decision: JFC 2026-10-05: shell freeze lifted; approved capabilities must not regress without an explicit product decision.
coverage: Initial protected inventory. Passing these tests is not proof of complete UI/UX coverage or physical-device health.

capabilities.contract: Any money view with a balance due (Commissions by product incl. product sheet, Commissions by rack, Customers fiado incl. Pending payment filter, dashboard commissions) shows a visible, enabled, 44px+ control in the active language to record that payment, also with integrity pending. Unresolved conflicting payment receipts and confirmed overpayments retain visible review evidence and guard further disbursements against that ambiguity.

changeApproval.reason: JFC explicitly requested repairs and guards for all five reproduced monetary failures, including concurrent overpayments and conflicting payment intentions. No receipt is discarded or selected as financially valid.
changeApproval.previousContract: Any money view with a balance due (Commissions by product incl. product sheet, Commissions by rack, Customers fiado incl. Pending payment filter, dashboard commissions) shows a visible, enabled, 44px+ control in the active language to record that payment, also with integrity pending.

capabilities.contract: Earned/Paid/Still due, partial payments, statements, history, person and shelf editors and historical deep links remain reachable.
The four monthly commission totals open readable breakdowns; product/person editors and explicit period payment routes remain usable in EN/ES, Chromium and WebKit.
Both product/SKU and rack/event views remain available.

Selected period survives dashboard-to-app payment navigation. Product payment opens the existing product sheet and restricts payouts to selected product sales/person/rack; grouped rack payment remains reachable.

changeApproval.reason: JFC requested product and rack settlement separately and correction of the product button redirect to grouped racks, preserving the approved payout architecture.
changeApproval.previousContract: Selected period survives dashboard-to-app payment navigation.

capabilities.contract: Counter is a sales channel, never implicit removal of the piece/shelf commission.
New payments are exact, auditable facts; partial payments, retries and legacy history remain coherent.
Split and return adjustments preserve paid history.
Archived or deleted shelves do not reappear from stale peers.
Rendering preserves photos; recovery uses exact shelf evidence and respects newer images.
Exports are importable and preserve photo evidence; corrupt imports do not erase business state.
Business edits converge without mixing tenants or applying operations twice.
Stale legacy zero cannot erase valid positive stock; legitimate modern zero remains supported.
Undo and returns preserve the existing accounting and stock semantics.
Changing display language does not overwrite the user's business name.

El dinero se deriva en tres capas (hechos, libro de doble entrada, vistas): cada asiento suma cero, el saldo de 2000 por persona = Pendiente al centavo, el libro es determinista e idempotente (ADR-001).

Paid sale cancellation remains recoverable in later periods; legacy payments, consumption and reversals remain coherent. Exported payouts use backwards-readable item kinds and preserve the logical recovery identity.

Commission payments, reversals and legacy multi-person batches confirm complete durable storage before success or sync notification. Failed attempts restore financial facts and preserve photo evidence; retries remain idempotent.
Payment controls announce full/partial choice in EN/ES before clicking; partial payments refresh the local dashboard to the same cents without changing stock or losing period links.
Local device nickname edits report immediately; passive checkins cannot rewind confirmed business/device names from stale KV into the fresh registry; folded device nicknames remain searchable.
The PIN badge describes the controlling worker, not whichever cache is newest.

An activated business, including lord, starts and stays empty when it has no owner-created records. Optional sales demo remains separate. Exact historical demo fingerprints are excluded from app/dashboard/shared catalog without deleting recoverable storage or real transaction history. No sample-rack label or workaround copy is imposed on business data.

Customer payments retain a durable intention across response loss/reload; retries do not receive the same money twice. Settled accounts keep receipts visible. Identity changes do not corrupt fact chains; real missing evidence remains unverified.

Expenses confirm complete durable storage; failed creates/edits/voids restore the prior state. Actual payout cents and excess remain visible. Conflicting receipts converge as retained evidence excluded from verified journal postings; malformed or role-incompatible incoming payments remain separately recoverable. Role metadata is a compatibility guard, not cryptographic authorization.

Unchanged owner business-name metadata produces no Yjs updates on periodic reseeds. A real rename still converges and a stale name cannot rewind it. This guard measures client updates, not total billed relay writes or physical-device latency.

Sold and Dashboard share a read-only sales history with date, rack/event and product filters, quantities, unit prices and exact cents. Identified cash, credit and unspecified methods remain distinct; the report never claims a cash drawer balance or writes financial facts.

Browsers with Web Locks keep a second app tab usable and serialize each API write against the latest durable state. Concurrent last-unit sales permit one sale; independent sales survive reload. Without cross-tab locks, the compatibility guard rejects secondary-tab mutations and offers no unsafe override. A saved local dashboard admits owner/admin access with the app closed and does not require another open app tab.

changeApproval.reason: JFC requires seamless tab changes, warnings only for a real data-loss risk, and records the old keep-app-open requirement as vestigial for independent local access.
changeApproval.previousContract: A lifetime session lock blocks a second app tab even when API writes already use Web Locks; a legacy UI override permits bypassing that warning.

capabilities.contract: A new authenticated app session closes the previous app session in the same notebook after an executing write completes; queued stale-session writes are rejected. Local durable updates refresh active views directly without relay debounce. The closed session offers PIN resume, onboarding tips and sharing only the public app URL, with no false delivery or clipboard confirmation.

Dashboard payment and correction links open the existing same-origin app editor in an embedded dialog while the parent remains in dashboard.html. Product, rack and selected month survive native PIN login; no credentials travel in the URL. Existing permissions and the payout ledger govern writes. Closing returns to the refreshed report; changing notebooks closes both report and editor.

changeApproval.reason: JFC explicitly requires the dashboard to use an embed and never take the user away to the app.
changeApproval.previousContract: Dashboard payment and correction links navigate the parent page to index.html and its native editors.
